recommendation: Keep the commit as-is; it completes the narrow FHIR-7924 removal while preserving later async-only Content-Location documentation. Handle any broader HTTP header modernization under a separate tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-7924 asked how read responses should populate Content-Location when a server does not support full versioning; the Published/Not Persuasive with Modification resolution was to remove the Content-Location header from the read guidance instead.
initial_application: Git commit a3d92167cec3c317028c952cd87d533034ec6589 (SVN r6510, '#7924 - remove content-location header') removed the explicit Content-Location response guidance from the REST metadata map, read/vread/update/create/conformance prose, and interaction summary table, but left an older vread sentence that still said a version id could come from a content location returned from read.
additional_context: source/http.html is active build-scope source via publish.ini. Later FHIR-38991 commits added and corrected a Content-Location row in the HTTP header table for the async pattern only, so that table entry should remain. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision requiring Content-Location on read responses.
reconciliation: Edited source/http.html in the vread section so the version id may be recorded from the ETag returned from read, aligning the paragraph with the metadata table and current read interaction text.
source_changes: source/http.html: replaced the stale 'content location returned from a read' vread phrase with 'ETag returned from a read'.

related_jiras.note: Later added Location and Content-Location to the HTTP headers table; Content-Location is scoped to the async pattern and constrains this reconciliation to the stale read/vread wording.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Not Persuasive with Modification issue requesting clarification for read Content-Location when versioning is unsupported; the accepted resolution was to remove the Content-Location header.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final FHIR-I decision that read response guidance should not depend on Content-Location.

evidence_items.summary: The initial #7924 implementation removed Content-Location from the REST metadata mapping, read/vread/update/create/conformance prose, and interaction summary table.
evidence_items.learned: Most of the accepted change was already applied, but the older vread discovery sentence was not removed by that patch.

evidence_items.summary: The active HTTP page read text uses ETag and Last-Modified, while the vread paragraph still referred to a content location returned from read before this reconciliation.
evidence_items.learned: The remaining stale wording was in current build-scope source and directly affected implementer understanding of read/vread version discovery.

evidence_items.summary: Later FHIR-38991 work added and corrected the Content-Location row in the HTTP headers table for the async pattern.
evidence_items.learned: The current async Content-Location table row has a separate later basis and should not be removed as part of FHIR-7924.
